messages.author: d3fd439c2e48caf1
messages.subject: Zero-inflation and overdispersion in pcountOpen
parts:
I know it's much too late on a Friday, but I'm looking for some suggestions on dealing with zero-inflated (>50% of observations) counts with large count numbers (max = 55).

From what I can tell, ZINB models aren't currently implemented in pcountOpen and I was considering a zero-inflated poisson model using something like ceiling(y/5) to get the count distribution near to ZIP. From there I thought I could multiply parameter estimates or BUPs by 5 to return them to near their original scale. This is optimistic logic, I admit. Does this sound reasonable, or can someone offer an alternative approach? I've played around with this data in glmmADMB (which [sometimes] accomodates ZINB), but I'm optimistic about pcountOpen in unmarked.

Thanks in advance,
Giancarlo

messages.author: 2a3a0c6a456f3043
messages.subject: Re: Zero-inflation and overdispersion in pcountOpen
parts:
Hi Giancarlo,

I would be curious to hear more about the distribution of your counts on two levels. First, what is the distribution of your counts across sites and secondly what is your distribution of counts within sites? Also, how many sites to you have? Open abundance models like those implemented in pcountOpen tend to require a very large number of sites for convergence. Adding in challenges of zero inflation and overdispersion might make fitting your data in pcountOpen difficult. I have had more success with these models using the autoreg option in dynamics. In terms of your original question, I think seeing a distribution of counts by site in the form of histograms would be helpful for determining if the data are likely to fit a ZIP model (i.e. within sites does it look Poisson distributed other than the zeros). Either way it's difficult to know when the data will fit a particular distribution because the distributions are after the covariates are accounted for (lambda is Poisson distributed and lambda = exp(a + b1*x1 + ... + bn*xn).

I am a bit skeptical about the idea of using y/5 and then multiplying estimates by 5. One problem would be that any counts not evenly divisible by 5 would not be integers and a Poisson distribution expects integers.

Ideally you would have covariates that could explain any extra Poisson variation on the upper end of the distribution and a zero-inflation factor to account for extra zeros. Then you could use a ZIP model without a problem. I have found that negative binomial models generate biologically unrealistic estimates, particularly in the upper 95% CI estimates of N[i]. It could be better to use an imperfect ZIP model than an unrealistic but good fitting ZINB model when you have large mean non-zero counts.

Sorry, that get's rather far afield of your original question but hopefully it gives you some things to try over the weekend.
Cheers,
Dan

messages.author: d3fd439c2e48caf1
messages.subject: Re: Zero-inflation and overdispersion in pcountOpen
parts:
Hi Dan, thanks for taking the time to consider my flawed logic and for your helpful perspectives.

This data is from 42 years of lek counts (1 count/lek/year) of a prairie grouse at 255 leks.  I've trimmed the set to 88 leks having >= 10 counts and >= 30 years between the first and last surveys per lek.  Counts are highly dynamic and are confounded by local population health/habitat and detection issues (to which we can all relate!). I'm primarily interested in overall estimates of recruitment and survival and, currently, have no other site covariates other than the obvious site-year and/or detection covariate of count year.

I've made some .png files and some descriptive stats of distributions

All data: http://wp.me/a31SIX-3C
1,802 counts, 990 (55%) zeros, mean = 4.7, variance = 45.4, max = 40.

Across-lek summary: http://wp.me/a31SIX-3B
1. A mean 58% (SE = 3%) of counts within leks were zero counts.
2. The mean mean count was 4.3 (SE = 0.4) (includes zeros)
3. The mean max count was 15.5 (SE = 0.8).  17 leks had a max count over 20, five leks had a max count over 30.
4. The mean # of counts within sites was 20.5 (SE = 0.7)

So, to the last point, I haven't found previous discussion of missing data (which is about 50% in this data set) in running Dail-Madsen / pcountOpen models. I know some of the other unmarked-implemented models (e.g. colext) are flexible about missing data and I'd be very interested to hear from anyone (Richard?) about any issues associated with with missing observations in pcountOpen.

I have been experimenting with the different distributions (and different K values) using the autoregressive dynamic and an intercept-only model and have found the NB distribution to have a far lower AIC than P or ZIP models (ZIP models being nearly 2 AIC > than P models).  Perhaps the extra zeros aren't an issue here or are being accounted for in the detection component of the model (?).  I've been upping the K from 50 to 100 to 200 (with ever-increasing calculation times) and estimates continue to improve.  Parameter estimates, predictions (just linear combs at this point), and BUPs look reasonable.  This is as far as I've gone with this, mostly due to the time required when K = 200+.  I hope to eventually include year-specific detection, recruitment and/or survival. 

Thanks again, Dan, and all else who offer insight/suggestions here.

Giancarlo
